questions.question: Which dispatcher does `viewModelScope.launch { }` use when you don't pass one?
options: `Dispatchers.Main.immediate`
`Dispatchers.IO`
`Dispatchers.Default`
`Dispatchers.Unconfined`
questions.explanation: `viewModelScope` is built from `SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Main.immediate`, so code runs on the main thread, and runs right away if you're already on it. Blocking IO has to be moved off with `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)` or a main-safe suspend API such as Room or Retrofit.

questions.question: `scope.cancel()` plays the role of `onCleared()` here. What does this print?
options:
cleanup
cancelled=true

cleanup
late
cancelled=true

loaded
cleanup
cancelled=false
cancelled=true
questions.explanation: Cancelling the scope cancels its running child, so `delay` throws `CancellationException` and only the `finally` block runs. A cancelled scope's job stays cancelled, so a later `launch` in it never runs. That is why you can't reuse `viewModelScope` after `onCleared()`.

questions.question: An Activity's `lifecycleScope` is cancelled when the lifecycle reaches DESTROYED, not when the Activity is merely stopped.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: `lifecycleScope` is tied to the whole lifecycle and is cancelled only at DESTROYED. Coroutines launched in it keep running while the app is in the background, which is why flow collection needs `repeatOnLifecycle` on top of it.

questions.question: A ViewModel starts a network call in `viewModelScope` and exposes the result as a `StateFlow`. The user rotates the screen while it's loading. What happens?
options: The call keeps running and the new Activity gets the result from the same `StateFlow`
The call is cancelled and started again when the new Activity is created
The call keeps running, but its result is lost because the old Activity was destroyed
The app crashes because the coroutine still references the destroyed Activity
questions.explanation: A ViewModel survives configuration changes, so `viewModelScope` isn't cancelled. `onCleared()` only runs when the owner goes away for good. The new Activity gets the same ViewModel and collects the latest state.

questions.question: Which statements about `viewModelScope` are true?
options: It is cancelled when the ViewModel's `onCleared()` runs
It uses a `SupervisorJob`, so one failing child doesn't cancel its siblings
It survives configuration changes such as rotation
It is cancelled whenever the hosting Activity goes to the background
You must cancel it yourself in `onDestroy()` to avoid leaks
questions.explanation: `viewModelScope` lives exactly as long as the ViewModel and is cancelled automatically when it is cleared, so you never cancel it yourself. Going to the background (STOP) doesn't clear a ViewModel.

questions.question: This scope is built like `viewModelScope` (a `SupervisorJob` plus a handler). What does it print?
options:
caught boom
b done
active=true

caught boom
active=false

caught boom
b done
active=false

b done
caught boom
active=true
questions.explanation: With a `SupervisorJob`, a failing child doesn't cancel its siblings or the scope, so `b` still finishes and the scope stays active. With a plain `Job`, the failure would cancel `b` and the scope, which would be fatal for a ViewModel running several independent loads.

questions.question: Why was `lifecycleScope.launchWhenStarted { locationFlow.collect { ... } }` deprecated in favour of `repeatOnLifecycle`?
options: Below STARTED it only suspends the collector, so the upstream keeps running
It cancels the collector at STOP and never restarts it on START
It runs its block on a background thread, so updating views from it crashes
It is cancelled on rotation, unlike `repeatOnLifecycle`
questions.explanation: `launchWhenStarted` pauses the coroutine instead of cancelling it, so producers like `callbackFlow` stay registered and keep emitting into a buffer while the app is in the background. `repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED)` cancels the collection on STOP, which also stops the upstream.

questions.question: For work that must keep going after the user leaves a screen, `GlobalScope.launch` is the recommended approach on Android.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: `GlobalScope` has no owner, so nothing can cancel it or replace its dispatcher in tests. The recommended options are an app-wide `CoroutineScope` injected via DI, or WorkManager when the work must be guaranteed to finish even if the process dies.

questions.question: In Compose, what does `viewModel.uiState.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` do that `collectAsState()` doesn't?
options: It stops collecting below STARTED and resumes when the lifecycle is STARTED again
It keeps the collected value across process death
It collects on `Dispatchers.IO` instead of the main thread, so slow emissions don't cause jank
It caches the latest value in the ViewModel's `SavedStateHandle`
questions.explanation: `collectAsStateWithLifecycle` uses `repeatOnLifecycle` internally with `minActiveState = STARTED` by default. `collectAsState` keeps collecting as long as the composable is in the composition, including while the app is in the background.

questions.question: The app goes to the background (Activity reaches STOPPED). Which of these collections are cancelled, rather than suspended or left running?
options: `lifecycleScope.launch { repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) { flow.collect { ... } } }`
`lifecycleScope.launch { flow.flowWithLifecycle(lifecycle, Lifecycle.State.STARTED).collect { ... } }`
`val state by flow.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` in a composable
`lifecycleScope.launchWhenStarted { flow.collect { ... } }`
`lifecycleScope.launch { flow.collect { ... } }`
questions.explanation: `repeatOnLifecycle`, `flowWithLifecycle` and `collectAsStateWithLifecycle` all cancel the collection below STARTED and restart it on START. `launchWhenStarted` only suspends, and a plain `lifecycleScope.launch` keeps collecting until DESTROYED.

questions.question: The timeout stands in for the lifecycle stopping. What does this print?
options:
name=Ann
stopped

name=Ann
count=1
stopped

count=1
name=Ann
stopped
stopped
questions.explanation: Collecting a `StateFlow` never completes, so the first `collect` suspends until the timeout cancels it and the second line is never reached. The same thing happens inside one `repeatOnLifecycle` block, so each flow needs its own `launch`.

questions.question: What is `flow.flowWithLifecycle(lifecycle, Lifecycle.State.STARTED)` best described as?
options: An operator that collects upstream only while at least STARTED, like `repeatOnLifecycle`
A terminal operator that collects the flow by itself, so no coroutine is needed
An operator that buffers every value emitted while stopped and replays them all on START
A replacement for `viewModelScope` that ties the flow to the ViewModel
questions.explanation: `flowWithLifecycle` is built on `repeatOnLifecycle` and is handy when you have a single flow to collect. It returns a new `Flow`, so it still has to be collected from a coroutine, and it doesn't replay values the upstream emitted while stopped.

questions.question: `repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) { ... }` is a suspend call that doesn't return until the lifecycle is DESTROYED, so code written after it in the same coroutine only runs at that point.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: `repeatOnLifecycle` keeps re-running its block on every START and resumes the caller only once the lifecycle is destroyed. Code placed after it, such as another `collect`, effectively never runs while the screen is in use.

questions.question: When the user taps Send, a chat message must be written to the local DB and posted (about 1s), even if they immediately press back and the ViewModel is cleared. Surviving process death isn't required. What's the best place to launch this work?
options: An app-wide `CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob())` injected into the repository via DI
`GlobalScope.launch`, because it is never cancelled
The Activity's `lifecycleScope`, because it outlives the ViewModel and is only cancelled at process death
`runBlocking` inside `onCleared()` so the ViewModel waits for it
questions.explanation: An injected `applicationScope` outlives any one screen while staying owned, testable and replaceable in tests. `GlobalScope` can't be controlled, `lifecycleScope` is cancelled at DESTROYED, which happens on back, and `runBlocking` freezes the main thread. If the work had to survive process death, WorkManager would be the right tool.

questions.question: The `onItems` callback never fires. Which changes fix it?
options: Wrap each `collect` in its own `launch { }` inside the `repeatOnLifecycle` block
Use two separate `lifecycleScope.launch { repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED) { ... } }` blocks, one per flow
Swap the order of the two `collect` calls
Add `yield()` between the two `collect` calls
Replace `repeatOnLifecycle` with `launchWhenStarted`
questions.explanation: `header` is a `StateFlow`, so its `collect` never returns and the second line is never reached. Each collector needs its own coroutine. Swapping the order just starves `header` instead, and `yield()` or `launchWhenStarted` don't change the fact that `collect` suspends forever.

questions.question: A Fragment calls `lifecycleScope.launch { repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED) { vm.state.collect { binding.title.text = it } } }` in `onViewCreated`. The user navigates to another Fragment (this one goes on the back stack) and then presses back. What's the problem?
options: The Fragment isn't destroyed, so each return adds another collector that outlives its view
Nothing, because `lifecycleScope` in a Fragment already follows the view lifecycle
The collector is cancelled when the view is destroyed and never restarts after the user returns
The app crashes right away because `lifecycleScope` can't be used before `onStart`
questions.explanation: A Fragment on the back stack loses its view (`onDestroyView`) but the Fragment itself isn't destroyed, so its `lifecycleScope` lives on. Use `viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycleScope` and `viewLifecycleOwner.repeatOnLifecycle` for UI work, so the collector dies with the view and exactly one exists per view.

questions.question: Each loop iteration simulates START (launch) and STOP (cancel), like `repeatOnLifecycle`. What does this print?
questions.explanation: While "stopped" there is no collector, so the update to 2 isn't printed then. On the next START a fresh collector immediately gets the current `StateFlow` value (2), then 3. Restarting on START gives the UI the latest state without replaying what it missed.

questions.question: Which statements about coroutine scopes in Compose are true?
options: `LaunchedEffect(key)` cancels its coroutine and launches a new one when `key` changes
The scope from `rememberCoroutineScope()` is cancelled when that composable leaves the composition
`rememberCoroutineScope()` is the right way to start a coroutine from an `onClick` handler
`LaunchedEffect` can be called directly inside an `onClick` lambda
`rememberCoroutineScope()` survives configuration changes like `viewModelScope`
questions.explanation: `LaunchedEffect` is a composable tied to the composition and its keys, so it can't be called from a non-composable callback like `onClick`. Use `rememberCoroutineScope()` there. That scope is bound to the composition, so it's cancelled when the composable leaves it, and also on rotation, when the composition is rebuilt.

questions.question: An Activity calls `lifecycleScope.launch { repeatOnLifecycle(STARTED) { vm.events.collect { show(it) } } }` inside `onStart()` instead of `onCreate()`. After the user leaves the app and comes back twice, what happens?
options: Three collectors are active, because each call keeps restarting its block until DESTROYED
Exactly one collector is active, because `repeatOnLifecycle` cancels any earlier call
No collector is active, because `repeatOnLifecycle` called in `onStart` misses the START event
It throws `IllegalStateException`, because `repeatOnLifecycle` may only be called from `onCreate`
questions.explanation: `repeatOnLifecycle` only returns at DESTROYED and restarts its block on every START, so calling it from `onStart` stacks up a new restarting collector every time. Call it once from `onCreate` (or `onViewCreated` with `viewLifecycleOwner` in a Fragment).

questions.question: Because `viewModelScope` uses a `SupervisorJob`, an exception thrown inside `viewModelScope.launch { }` with no try/catch or handler is silently swallowed and the app keeps running.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: A `SupervisorJob` only stops the failure from cancelling siblings and the scope. The exception is still uncaught, so it goes to the thread's default uncaught exception handler, which crashes an Android app. Catch it in the coroutine or map it to an error state.
